angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 68,390,093 km at 118.06 pc = 7.74 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112961: distance 118.064 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.078), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 118.064 +/- 9.209 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.9360 +/- 0.2356 mas (same row, RUWE 3.10), 37.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 98.304 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112961: radius 98.304 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1630.73 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.103) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 68,390,093 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3702 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112961: effective temperature 3702 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.181) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112961: effective temperature 3702 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.181) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
